newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo says Lonrho mooted swap idea.
newsitem.headline: Anglo says Lonrho mooted swap idea.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Limited said on Wednesday Lonrho Plc had mooted a share-swap of Anglo's Lonrho stake for the Brisith company's interests in Ashanti Goldfields Ltd.
"The idea of possibly swapping our Lonrho shares for shares in Ashanti is an idea that came from the Lonrho side," Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said.
He told a presentation of the company's annual report that Anglo was in no hurry to resolve the issue of reducing its stake in Lonrho to less than 10 percent, as agreed with the European Commission.
"As far as we are concerned, we have two years to resolve it, so we are in no hurry to resolve this," Ogilvie Thompson said.
The European Union earlier this year said Anglo American had agreed to reduce its stake of around 27 percent in Lonrho.
The EU said before the agreement it considered the two companies' combined platinum interests as a monopoly.
Ogilvie Thompson said that contrary to market talk, Anglo was not behind a proposed of JCI Ltd with Lonrho.
He said the idea for the merger came from JCI, and especially its chairman, Mzi Khumalo.
"We are not running this thing," he said.
